A run cut mid-seal

You will learn

What a seal file holds after a run is killed, for each of three ways of writing it.

What if a run is killed while it writes a seal? seal_write.t27 asks it of 3 ways of writing and 4 moments of a cut. Writing in place and cutting during the write leaves a torn file. Writing and restoring leaves another spec's seal in place when the new seal belongs to a spec that derived the same file name. Staging the seal and renaming it leaves the old seal until the rename and the new checked one after it, at every one of the 4 moments. cut_safe accepts only those two states. The lab account of 2026-10-18 measured writing in place and writing then restoring; the third way is the rule.

Try it

Cut the in-place write during the write. Then pick write then restore and tick a foreign seal, and then pick stage then rename and look at every moment.

Open the interactive lesson →

Three ways to write a seal file, four moments a run can be cut, and one question: what does the file hold afterwards. Pick a way and a moment and see whether the file can be trusted.

specs/verified/seal_write.t27

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
; specs/verified/seal_write.t27 -- what one seal write must guarantee before it may land in
; .trinity/seals/. The three write-safety patterns of REA 6.6.0 (github.com/morluto/rea releases),
; checked against `t27c seal --save` and `t27c frontier --reseal` on the Railway lab, t27c 0.5.2 at
; master 89254d2, 2026-10-18.
; --
; What already exists and is NOT restated here:
; - specs/verified/seal_identity.t27 says when a new seal is kept (remint_keeps) and names the
;   colliding file name: two specs can derive one seal file (parent dir and module), and frontier
;   writes the other spec's seal back. `seal --save` itself never refuses. This file is the write.
; - specs/verified/seal_check.t27 says how a seal is checked later from recorded inputs. This file
;   is the check the writer owes before its seal can be checked at all.
; - specs/verified/reuse.t27 owns the PART_* codes and the fail-closed rule (MISSING is never SAME).
; --
; The three patterns, and where the pipeline stands (lab evidence: gHashTag/t27#10457):
; 1. Colliding paths are refused before any write -- MISSING. `seal --save specs/a/same/m.t27` then
;    `seal --save specs/b/same/m.t27` (both `module SameName;`) both exit 0, "Seal saved to
;    .trinity/seals/same_SameName.json"; the file then names specs/b, and `seal --verify` of specs/a
;    reports all five hashes MISMATCH. `module Upper;` in c/case and `module upper;` in d/case collide
;    the same way, through the case-insensitive lookup. The corpus has 8 such names over 2198 specs.
; 2. The hash is re-checked after the final write -- MISSING. The spec is hashed once, before its
;    tests read it again. A failing spec swapped for a passing one 0-4 ms into `seal --save`, then
;    swapped back, sealed "tests 1/1 pass" under the FAILING bytes' spec_hash in 14 of 18 trials;
;    `seal --verify` said all hashes MATCH and `frontier --list` reused it (1000 permille) while
;    `test-report` on those bytes fails. An edit during the test run left a seal whose spec_hash
;    mismatched the moment it was written; `seal --save` still said "Seal saved" and exited 0.
; 3. Completed seals survive a cut run -- PRESENT for completed seals. SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGKILL
;    6 s into a frontier reseal of six specs left 4, 2 and 3 finished seals, each verifying, and no
;    partial file. The seal in flight is not safe: frontier writes first and restores from a copy
;    held only in the parent's memory, so killing the parent while its child wrote specs/b's seal
;    into specs/a's file left specs/a failing verification for good.
; --
; The write rule:
; - The destination is free only when no file answers to its name (case-insensitively, as the
;   lookup does), or the file there records exactly this spec_path. A file whose owner cannot be
;   read is not free: fail closed, as reuse.t27 does for an unrecorded part. --force opens an
;   unreadable owner and never another spec's file (dest_allowed, #10454).
; - After the seal is written to a staging file, the spec is hashed again and must equal the
;   recorded spec_hash; the tests must have run on the bytes that hash names; the staged file read
;   back must equal what was written; the spec generated again must give the recorded gen hashes
;   (gens_check). Any difference refuses the seal and leaves the old one.
; - The staged, checked file then replaces the old one by one rename. A cut at any point leaves
;   the old seal or the new checked seal, never a torn file, an unchecked seal or another spec's.
; Tests pin literal codes where a code names itself, so renumbering the constants cannot pass.
; phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY

module VerifiedSealWrite;

use verified::reuse;

/// dest_check() and post_write_check() answers.
pub const WRITE_OK : u8 = 0;
pub const WRITE_COLLISION : u8 = 1;
pub const WRITE_OWNER_UNKNOWN : u8 = 2;
pub const WRITE_SPEC_MOVED : u8 = 3;
pub const WRITE_TESTED_OTHER : u8 = 4;
pub const WRITE_READBACK_DIFF : u8 = 5;
/// gens_check(): the spec held still, but generating it again gave other code, so the seal would
/// record a gen hash nobody can reproduce.
pub const WRITE_GEN_MOVED : u8 = 6;

/// The staging file is `.<seal name><SEAL_STAGE_SUFFIX>-<pid>` beside the seal. Seal readers take
/// only `*.json`, so a staged file a cut left behind is never read as a seal.
pub const SEAL_STAGE_SUFFIX : str = ".part";

/// How a seal reaches its file.
/// IN_PLACE: `seal --save` today, fs::write straight onto the destination.
/// WRITE_THEN_RESTORE: `frontier --reseal` today, the child writes in place and the parent writes
/// the old text back from memory when remint_keeps() refuses the new seal.
/// STAGE_THEN_RENAME: the rule above.
pub const PROTO_IN_PLACE : u8 = 1;
pub const PROTO_WRITE_THEN_RESTORE : u8 = 2;
pub const PROTO_STAGE_THEN_RENAME : u8 = 3;

/// Where a run can be cut while it seals one spec.
pub const CUT_BEFORE_WRITE : u8 = 1;
pub const CUT_DURING_WRITE : u8 = 2;
pub const CUT_AFTER_WRITE : u8 = 3;
pub const CUT_AFTER_COMMIT : u8 = 4;

/// What the destination file holds after the cut.
pub const DISK_OLD : u8 = 1;
pub const DISK_NEW_CHECKED : u8 = 2;
pub const DISK_NEW_UNCHECKED : u8 = 3;
pub const DISK_TORN : u8 = 4;
pub const DISK_FOREIGN : u8 = 5;

/// Two derived seal file names name one file when they are equal or equal up to case: `--save`
/// matches an existing file case-insensitively, so case_Upper.json answers for `module upper;`.
/// Why the lookup folds case (moved here from run_seal, #10457): macOS resolves
/// ar_restraint.json and ar_Restraint.json to one file and hides the difference, while on the
/// case-sensitive filesystem CI runs on, `--save` would create a SECOND seal for the same spec and
/// neither would look wrong. Measured over the store: 751 file names match the derived name
/// exactly, 4 differ only by case, 558 use the older bare-<module> scheme. An existing file wins,
/// so the store cannot grow a case-variant twin; dest_check() then says whose file it is.
pub fn names_collide(exact_equal: bool, casefold_equal: bool) -> bool {
    if (exact_equal) { return true; }
    return casefold_equal;
}

/// May this spec's seal be written to its derived file? dest_exists covers a case-variant name;
/// owner_known says the existing file's spec_path could be read; owner_is_this_spec compares it.
pub fn dest_check(dest_exists: bool, owner_known: bool, owner_is_this_spec: bool) -> u8 {
    if (dest_exists == false) { return WRITE_OK; }
    if (owner_known == false) { return WRITE_OWNER_UNKNOWN; }
    if (owner_is_this_spec) { return WRITE_OK; }
    return WRITE_COLLISION;
}

/// `seal --save` today: it writes whatever is at the destination. Kept as the unsafe reference the
/// negative controls compare against.
pub fn dest_check_today(dest_exists: bool, owner_known: bool, owner_is_this_spec: bool) -> u8 {
    return WRITE_OK;
}

/// The check after the staged write. Hashes are stand-ins for the recorded sha256 values, compared
/// whole: recorded is the spec_hash in the seal, after is the spec hashed again once the seal is
/// staged, tested is the hash of the bytes the test run read. readback_equal says the staged file
/// read back equals the text that was written.
pub fn post_write_check(recorded: u64, after: u64, tested: u64, readback_equal: bool) -> u8 {
    if (tested != recorded) { return WRITE_TESTED_OTHER; }
    if (after != recorded) { return WRITE_SPEC_MOVED; }
    if (readback_equal == false) { return WRITE_READBACK_DIFF; }
    return WRITE_OK;
}

/// May `seal --save` write, given dest_check()'s answer? A collision is another spec's seal and
/// nothing lifts it, --force included: forcing would only move the damage to the other spec. An
/// unknown owner is a file that does not parse (a torn write from before staging) or a legacy seal
/// with no spec_path; the writer cannot prove it is someone else's, so it stays closed unless the
/// person sealing says --force.
pub fn dest_allowed(code: u8, force: bool) -> bool {
    if (code == WRITE_OK) { return true; }
    if (code == WRITE_OWNER_UNKNOWN) { return force; }
    return false;
}

/// The gen half of the check after the staged write: post_write_check()'s answer stands when it
/// refuses; otherwise the four gen hashes computed again must equal the ones recorded.
pub fn gens_check(code: u8, gens_same: bool) -> u8 {
    if (code != WRITE_OK) { return code; }
    if (gens_same) { return WRITE_OK; }
    return WRITE_GEN_MOVED;
}

/// `seal --save` today: no check after the write. The unsafe reference.
pub fn post_write_check_today(recorded: u64, after: u64, tested: u64, readback_equal: bool) -> u8 {
    return WRITE_OK;
}

/// What the destination holds when a run sealing one spec is cut at `cut`. foreign says the new
/// seal belongs to a different spec that derived the same file name (pattern 1 not yet refused).
pub fn after_cut(proto: u8, cut: u8, foreign: bool) -> u8 {
    if (cut == CUT_BEFORE_WRITE) { return DISK_OLD; }
    if (proto == PROTO_STAGE_THEN_RENAME) {
        // the rename is the commit: before it the destination was never touched
        if (cut == CUT_AFTER_COMMIT) { return DISK_NEW_CHECKED; }
        return DISK_OLD;
    }
    if (cut == CUT_DURING_WRITE) { return DISK_TORN; }
    if (foreign) {
        // write-then-restore restores only after the child exits; in place never restores
        if (proto == PROTO_WRITE_THEN_RESTORE) {
            if (cut == CUT_AFTER_COMMIT) { return DISK_OLD; }
        }
        return DISK_FOREIGN;
    }
    return DISK_NEW_UNCHECKED;
}

/// A cut is survivable when the file holds the old seal or the new checked one.
pub fn cut_safe(disk: u8) -> bool {
    if (disk == DISK_OLD) { return true; }
    return disk == DISK_NEW_CHECKED;
}

/// A protocol is cut-safe when every cut point leaves a survivable file, for its own spec and for a
/// spec that derived the same name.
pub fn proto_cut_safe(proto: u8) -> bool {
    if (cut_safe(after_cut(proto, CUT_DURING_WRITE, false)) == false) { return false; }
    if (cut_safe(after_cut(proto, CUT_AFTER_WRITE, false)) == false) { return false; }
    if (cut_safe(after_cut(proto, CUT_AFTER_WRITE, true)) == false) { return false; }
    if (cut_safe(after_cut(proto, CUT_AFTER_COMMIT, false)) == false) { return false; }
    return cut_safe(after_cut(proto, CUT_AFTER_COMMIT, true));
}

test a_free_or_own_destination_is_written {
    // a spec sealed for the first time
    assert dest_check(false, false, false) == 0;
    // a reseal of the spec's own seal
    assert dest_check(true, true, true) == 0;
}

test the_lab_collision_is_refused_before_any_write {
    // specs/b/same/m.t27 into same_SameName.json, which records specs/a/same/m.t27
    assert dest_check(true, true, false) == 1;
    // `module upper;` in d/case into case_Upper.json, which records c/case: the name lookup is
    // case-insensitive, so the destination exists
    assert names_collide(false, true) == true;
    assert dest_check(names_collide(false, true), true, false) == 1;
    // two names that differ beyond case are two files
    assert names_collide(false, false) == false;
}

test an_unreadable_owner_fails_closed {
    // a file that answers to the name but records no readable spec_path is nobody's to overwrite
    assert dest_check(true, false, false) == 2;
    assert dest_check(true, false, true) == 2;
}

test negative_control_today_writes_the_collision {
    // today's save says OK where the rule refuses. If the rule is ever weakened to today's, these
    // two lines stop differing and this test fails.
    assert dest_check_today(true, true, false) == WRITE_OK;
    assert dest_check(true, true, false) != dest_check_today(true, true, false);
    assert dest_check(true, false, false) != dest_check_today(true, false, false);
}

test negative_control_refusing_every_existing_file_is_wrong_too {
    // a rule that refuses any existing file would block every reseal; the own-seal case must pass
    assert dest_check(true, true, true) == WRITE_OK;
}

test the_written_seal_names_the_bytes_it_tested {
    // nothing moved: hashed, tested and re-hashed bytes agree and the read-back matches
    assert post_write_check(0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, true) == 0;
}

test the_lab_swap_is_refused {
    // 14 of 18 trials: spec_hash of the failing bytes (eef95aea...), tests run on the passing
    // bytes, the failing bytes back on disk by the time the seal is written
    assert post_write_check(0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, 0x2b, true) == 4;
}

test an_edit_during_the_tests_is_refused {
    // hashed and tested the same bytes, but the spec changed before the write: stale on arrival
    assert post_write_check(0xeef95aea, 0x3c, 0xeef95aea, true) == 3;
}

test a_short_or_torn_write_is_refused {
    assert post_write_check(0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, false) == 5;
}

test negative_control_today_seals_the_swap {
    // today's save says OK to the forged certificate the lab produced. Weaken the rule to today's
    // and these lines fail.
    assert post_write_check_today(0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, 0x2b, true) == WRITE_OK;
    assert post_write_check(0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, 0x2b, true) != WRITE_OK;
    assert post_write_check(0xeef95aea, 0x3c, 0xeef95aea, true) != WRITE_OK;
    assert post_write_check(0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, false) != WRITE_OK;
}

test negative_control_a_check_of_the_hash_alone_misses_the_swap {
    // re-hashing the spec after the write is not enough on its own: in the swap trials the
    // failing bytes were back, so after == recorded; only the tested-bytes check catches it
    var recorded : u64 = 0xeef95aea;
    var after : u64 = 0xeef95aea;
    assert after == recorded;
    assert post_write_check(recorded, after, 0x2b, true) == WRITE_TESTED_OTHER;
}

test stage_then_rename_survives_every_cut {
    assert proto_cut_safe(PROTO_STAGE_THEN_RENAME) == true;
    assert after_cut(PROTO_STAGE_THEN_RENAME, CUT_DURING_WRITE, false) == DISK_OLD;
    assert after_cut(PROTO_STAGE_THEN_RENAME, CUT_AFTER_WRITE, true) == DISK_OLD;
    assert after_cut(PROTO_STAGE_THEN_RENAME, CUT_AFTER_COMMIT, false) == DISK_NEW_CHECKED;
}

test negative_control_todays_protocols_do_not {
    // seal --save: fs::write in place, no check after it
    assert proto_cut_safe(PROTO_IN_PLACE) == false;
    assert after_cut(PROTO_IN_PLACE, CUT_DURING_WRITE, false) == DISK_TORN;
    assert after_cut(PROTO_IN_PLACE, CUT_AFTER_COMMIT, true) == DISK_FOREIGN;
    // frontier --reseal: the lab kill of the parent while its child wrote specs/b into specs/a's
    // file left specs/a's file naming specs/b
    assert proto_cut_safe(PROTO_WRITE_THEN_RESTORE) == false;
    assert after_cut(PROTO_WRITE_THEN_RESTORE, CUT_AFTER_WRITE, true) == DISK_FOREIGN;
    // when the parent lives to restore, the old seal is back (the lab control: "kept the old seal")
    assert after_cut(PROTO_WRITE_THEN_RESTORE, CUT_AFTER_COMMIT, true) == DISK_OLD;
}

test a_cut_never_reaches_back {
    // pattern 3: each spec has its own file, so a cut while sealing one spec leaves every other
    // spec where the run left it. A spec not reached yet is at CUT_BEFORE_WRITE under any protocol,
    // and a finished one was committed before the cut. SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGKILL after 6 s left
    // 4, 2 and 3 finished seals, all verifying.
    assert after_cut(PROTO_IN_PLACE, CUT_BEFORE_WRITE, true) == DISK_OLD;
    assert after_cut(PROTO_WRITE_THEN_RESTORE, CUT_BEFORE_WRITE, true) == DISK_OLD;
    assert after_cut(PROTO_STAGE_THEN_RENAME, CUT_BEFORE_WRITE, true) == DISK_OLD;
}

test force_lifts_an_unknown_owner_and_never_a_collision {
    // a free or own destination needs no force
    assert dest_allowed(dest_check(false, false, false), false) == true;
    assert dest_allowed(dest_check(true, true, true), false) == true;
    // a torn or legacy seal (owner unreadable) stays closed until the person sealing says --force
    assert dest_allowed(WRITE_OWNER_UNKNOWN, false) == false;
    assert dest_allowed(WRITE_OWNER_UNKNOWN, true) == true;
    // another spec's seal: --force does not open it
    assert dest_allowed(WRITE_COLLISION, true) == false;
    assert dest_allowed(dest_check(true, true, false), true) == false;
}

test negative_control_force_for_everything_would_reopen_the_collision {
    // a rule where --force lifts every refusal agrees on the unknown owner and differs only on the
    // collision; if dest_allowed is ever weakened to that, this line fails
    assert dest_allowed(WRITE_COLLISION, true) != dest_allowed(WRITE_OWNER_UNKNOWN, true);
}

test a_second_generation_must_give_the_recorded_code {
    assert gens_check(WRITE_OK, true) == 0;
    assert gens_check(WRITE_OK, false) == 6;
    // the spec check speaks first: a moved spec is reported as moved, not as moved gens
    assert gens_check(post_write_check(0xeef95aea, 0x3c, 0xeef95aea, true), false) == 3;
    assert gens_check(post_write_check(0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, 0x2b, true), true) == 4;
}

test negative_control_the_spec_check_alone_misses_moved_gens {
    // nothing about the spec moved, so post_write_check says OK; only gens_check refuses
    assert post_write_check(0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, true) == WRITE_OK;
    assert gens_check(post_write_check(0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, 0xeef95aea, true), false) != WRITE_OK;
}

test the_stage_suffix_is_not_a_seal_name {
    // readers take *.json; the staged name ends in SEAL_STAGE_SUFFIX-<pid>, never in .json
    assert SEAL_STAGE_SUFFIX == ".part";
    assert SEAL_STAGE_SUFFIX != ".json";
}
